business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Aseptic Barista-Formula Hydrolyzed Oat Milk

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain-China Double Taxation Agreement signed on 22 November 1990 and entered into force on 12 March 1991
Spain-United States Double Taxation Convention signed on 22 February 1990 and effective as of 1 January 1991
Spain-Mexico Double Taxation Agreement in force since 1994
Spain-Argentina Bilateral Investment Treaty signed in 1991 and in force since 1992
EU-Mexico Global Agreement in force since 1 July 2000

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio), Articles 20-22 (incorporation), 62-63 (registered office), 209-210 (board resolutions)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) and Provincial Registros Mercantiles
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) executed before a Notary and subsequently registered in the Registro Mercantil
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital of €3,000 (approx. USD 3,300) fully subscribed and paid up at incorporation; capital must be deposited in a Spanish bank account and blocked until registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the company subscribes and pays for the shares issued to the founding members as per the incorporation deed. That the registered office is established at [address] in Spain. That the following officers are appointed: [Name] as Managing Director, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer. That the officers are authorized to execute all necessary filings with the Commercial Registry, tax authorities, and other regulatory bodies. That the company shall open a corporate bank account and deposit the minimum capital. That the officers shall obtain all required industrial and environmental licenses for the operation of the UHT oat milk plant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request via the online portal or in person, providing up to five proposed company names. Obtain the 'certificado negativo de denominación' confirming the name is not already registered.
required_dossiers: Proposed company names in order of preference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the registry will indicate the reason; submit a revised application with alternative names within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notario) in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the public deed before a notary, including the bylaws, capital structure, share allocation, and appointment of initial directors. The notary will verify the legality and authenticity of the documents.
required_dossiers: Bank deposit certificate for the minimum capital
Identification documents of all founding members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, correct the deed and re-execute; any missing documents must be provided before signing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Registro Mercantil corresponding to the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized deed and supporting documents with the Provincial Registry for registration. Pay the applicable registration fee and obtain the registration certificate (inscripción).
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect notice, rectify the issues and resubmit within the given period (usually 15 days).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – local tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the provisional NIF (CIF) before registration, and then obtain the definitive NIF after registration. Submit the application via the AEAT online portal or in person.
required_dossiers: Registration certificate from the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is incomplete, AEAT will request additional documentation; provide within 10 days to avoid delays.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer with the TGSS to obtain an employer code (código de cuenta de cotización). This is required before hiring employees.
required_dossiers: Registration certificate from the Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If discrepancies are found, correct the data and resubmit; TGSS may require additional proof of corporate existence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Corporate Bank Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank (any authorized credit institution in Spain)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the name of the company and deposit the minimum capital (€3,000). Obtain a certificate of deposit from the bank, which is required for the notarization step.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional corporate documents, provide the registration certificate or notarized deed; if the account is delayed, use an alternative bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo (Ministry of Industry) and regional industrial authorities (e.g., Consejería de Industria of the autonomous community)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Actividad (Activity License) and Licencia de Apertura (Opening License) for the UHT plant and packaging facility

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) and regional environmental agencies (e.g., Consejería de Medio Ambiente)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – requires a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) for food processing plants with capacity > 50 tonnes/day; otherwise a simplified environmental authorization may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge limits per Real Decreto 817/2015 (max BOD5 25 mg/L, COD 125 mg/L, TSS 35 mg/L); VOC emissions per Real Decreto 117/2003 (limit 20 mg/m³); waste handling per Ley 22/2011 (hazardous waste classification and disposal protocols).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification per Real Decreto 2267/2004 (industrial fire protection); structural load inspections per Código Técnico de la Edificación (CTE); workplace safety clearance per Real Decreto 155/1997 (occupational health and safety) and Law 31/1995 (Prevención de Riesgos Laborales).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Sede Electrónica (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es). Responsible for VAT, TIN, and corporate income tax administration in Spain.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity with no permanent establishment in Spain that acquires a Spanish VAT registration must obtain a NIF-IVA (Número de Identificación Fiscal de Extranjero). The application is filed via form 036 (Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores) through AEAT's electronic office, or by submitting form 036 at a local AEAT office if no Spanish electronic certificate is held. The applicant must appoint a tax representative resident in Spain when required by AEAT, provide proof of identity and corporate existence, state the expected business commencement date, and register before any taxable supply is performed in Spain. Upon approval, AEAT issues the provisional NIF-IVA number. For a domestic Spanish SL entity, the NIF is obtained by depositing the deed of incorporation at the Commercial Registry, acquiring a provisional NIF (form 036/037), and then finalizing with the definitive NIF after registration. All registrations require a valid Spanish electronic ID, foreign entity certificate, or authorized signatory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; resident SL entities are taxed under Spain's corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at the standard 25% rate on worldwide income, unless the tax-credit system or territorial regime applies under specific provisions (e.g., ETVE regime, Canary Islands special zone).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not apply check-the-box classification for domestic entities; all Spanish incorporated SLs are automatically treated as taxable corporations. However, hybrid mismatch elections are restricted by the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) implemented in Spain. Non-resident entities can elect to operate through a permanent establishment (EP) by registering as such; a Spanish SL may opt to apply the Regímen Especial de Neutralidad Fiscal for mergers, spin-offs, and asset transfers. Multi-national groups may elect for the Spanish Group VAT Registration (Régimen del Grupo de Entidades – VAT grouping under the Spanish SII framework).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA) – VAT (Spanish Value Added Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic threshold applies to the registration of non-established foreign suppliers; a foreign entity carrying out taxable supplies in Spain must register from the first transaction. For intra-EU distance sales of goods, an annual turnover threshold of EUR 10,000 applies before the supply becomes taxable in Spain; the supplier must register for Spanish VAT once this threshold is exceeded, but may also voluntarily register below it. Spanish domestic small-business schemes do not provide a turnover-based exemption from VAT registration. A local Spanish SL has no VAT registration threshold and must register prior to commencing economic activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates electronic invoicing for businesses between private companies under the 'Crea y Crece' law (Law 18/2022). The mandate is phased; taxpayers subject to the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) regime (generally entities with annual turnover exceeding EUR 100 million, VAT groups, or those electing for SII) must submit VAT transaction records and invoice summaries to AEAT electronically within 4-8 days of each tax period using the AEAT web services and XSD schemas. There is no general real-time fiscal stamping for Spanish VAT; however, all taxpayers in continuous electronic invoicing must use an electronic invoicing system with a verifiable QR and signing structure per the Verifactum technical standard (for B2B invoices), and SII taxpayers receive a unique digital signature event code. Invoices must also be stored in the SII format, and software must comply with Regulation 1007/2023 which requires an integrity signature and an anti-fraud digital mark.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods shipped to a non-EU destination qualify for Spanish VAT export exemption at 0% when the seller proves that goods have physically left the EU within the statutory time limits (generally 90 days from shipment, extendable to 90 additional days under certain customs regimes). The exemption also covers goods destined for ship suppliers, armed forces, or tax-free shops under strict legal conditions. Supply of services to non-resident business customers is zero-rated for Spanish VAT when the recipient belongs outside the EU and the effective use and enjoyment occurs outside the EU, provided proper proof of recipient status is retained. The zero-rating requires an active VAT register, valid invoices, and the absence of fraud indicators in the supply chain.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA – Documento Único Administrativo) duly validated and accepted and released by Spanish Customs
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing actual physical movement of goods beyond the EU customs territory

Inward Remittance Certificate, bank credit advice, SWIFT MT103/TT wire receipt, or proof of export collection evidencing that the export proceeds have been received in Spain in accordance with the foreign-trade payment rules
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Spanish Tax Administration (AEAT) conducts rigorous export compliance audits, particularly reviewing the timely departure of goods, authentication of customs stamps, registration of export documentation, and consistency between export declarations, invoices, and bank receipts. False or fraudulent zero-rating claims result in retroactive VAT assessment (the 21% VAT being levied on the invoice), plus late-payment interest and surcharges. Proportional penalties may range from 50% to 150% of the scale where incorrect VAT is owed, based on the degree of concealment and fraud. In addition, customs penalties can be imposed under Spanish Customs Law, and criminal tax fraud under Art. 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code may apply when the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, carrying prison terms of 1-5 years for perpetrators. The exporter bears the burden of substantiation; any incomplete or internally inconsistent documents will cause the zero-rating to be disallowed and the tax clawed back.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem under the oversight framework of the European Central Bank; Spain's anti-money-laundering supervisory authority is the Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias and its Executive Service, SEPBLAC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro, which is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. No general exchange-control approval is required for capital contributions, shareholder loans, trade payments, dividends, interest, royalties, or liquidation proceeds. Cross-border transfers remain subject to bank transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, beneficial-ownership verification, tax compliance, transfer-pricing rules, corporate-law requirements, and applicable statistical or foreign-investment reporting. Profit remittance may be reduced by Spanish withholding tax unless an applicable tax treaty, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive regime, domestic exemption, or other statutory relief is available. Dividends must be distributable under Spanish corporate-law solvency and balance-sheet tests, and related-party financing must comply with arm's-length and interest-limitation rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement to repatriate export proceeds to Spain, surrender foreign-currency receipts, convert receipts into euros, or comply with a mandatory conversion ratio. No general statutory deadline applies to conversion of export proceeds. The company may retain proceeds in foreign-currency accounts, subject to contractual banking terms, accounting requirements, sanctions controls, tax reporting, and Banco de España statistical reporting where applicable. Export documentation, invoices, customs records, shipping evidence, and payment references should be retained to substantiate the commercial purpose and VAT treatment of receipts.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for supplementary collection, payment, and foreign-currency functionality; Low to Medium as the sole operating bank for a regulated food-manufacturing company. An offshore digital EMI cannot provide Spanish deposit-taking or Spanish payment services unless it is authorized in the European Economic Area or lawfully passported into Spain. EEA electronic-money institutions and payment institutions may operate through passporting or an authorized branch, subject to applicable PSD2, electronic-money, AML, safeguarding, outsourcing, and reporting requirements. Customer funds held by an EMI are safeguarded and are not equivalent to deposits covered by the Spanish deposit-guarantee scheme. The company should maintain a Spanish or EEA bank account for payroll, taxes, customs, regulated counterparties, capital evidence, and contingency liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal Spanish statutory requirement for all directors to appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the bank accepts qualified electronic identification, verified corporate documentation, reliable beneficial-owner evidence, and approved video or digital KYC procedures. Banks may nevertheless require a branch meeting, notarized or apostilled documents, a live video interview, Spanish tax identification numbers, specimen signatures, or an in-person appearance for non-resident directors, complex ownership chains, high-risk countries, unusual funding flows, or unresolved source-of-funds questions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or director with an opaque ownership chain, nominee arrangements, trusts, bearer-style documentation, or an unverified ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current corporate registry extracts for every ownership layer; constitutional documents; certified group ownership chart; passports and address evidence for all directors, authorized signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners; beneficial-owner declaration; notarized, apostilled, legalized, or electronically verifiable documents where required; and an explanation of control rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capitalization or shareholder funding received from an unrelated third party, newly incorporated foreign vehicle, high-risk jurisdiction, virtual-asset source, or unexplained personal account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital-increase or shareholder-loan agreement; board and shareholder resolutions; bank statements tracing funds to the originating party; audited or tax-supported source-of-wealth evidence; purchase agreements or sale-of-asset records where relevant; tax residency certificates; payment purpose narrative; and a funds-flow diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business activity involving food manufacturing, imported ingredients, packaging, cross-border sales, or projected transaction volumes inconsistent with the newly formed company's profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; plant lease or ownership evidence; food-production and environmental permits; supplier and customer contracts; import and export records; customs registrations; commercial invoices; logistics agreements; production-capacity estimates; forecast cash-flow statement; expected countries, currencies, counterparties, and monthly transaction volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned, embargoed, high-risk, or unusually structured jurisdictions, counterparties, vessels, banks, or intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty KYC files; sanctions-screening results; end-use and end-user statements; trade contracts; bills of lading; certificates of origin; customs declarations; beneficial-owner confirmations; screening methodology; escalation records; and documented legal review of any applicable EU, United Nations, United Kingdom, or United States sanctions exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected use of payment aggregators, offshore EMIs, virtual IBANs, nested accounts, cash-intensive collections, or third-party payment settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete payment-flow map; EMI or payment-institution license evidence; safeguarding and account-ownership confirmation; service agreement; reconciliation controls; segregation-of-funds procedures; counterparty onboarding policy; transaction-monitoring controls; and written explanation of why the structure is commercially necessary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete Spanish tax, corporate, or authorized-signatory documentation, including missing NIE, NIF, UBO, power-of-attorney, or registry evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish NIF documentation; NIE or equivalent identification for relevant individuals; current Registro Mercantil extracts; notarized powers of attorney; board resolutions; signature cards; tax-residency certificates; certified translations where requested; and a document-validity calendar.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume transfers without coherent invoice references, repeated round-number payments, rapid pass-through activity, or unexplained transfers between group entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy; payment-approval matrix; intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing policy; invoice-to-payment reconciliation; general-ledger extracts; cash-flow forecast; exception reports; documented economic rationale; and evidence that payment references match contracts, invoices, customs records, and delivery documentation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through a Spanish or EEA bank account in the company's legal name. For incorporation or a capital increase, use a bank certificate of deposit or equivalent evidence of funds where required by the notary and Registro Mercantil. For later contributions, obtain shareholder and board approvals, execute the capital-increase or shareholder-loan documentation, and ensure the accounting and corporate filings match the transfer. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments and SWIFT cross-border transfer for other currencies. Spain does not use a universal statutory FX purpose-code system comparable to certain controlled-currency jurisdictions; the payment should contain an accurate narrative and invoice, agreement, or capital-reference data. Banks may require a capital-increase deed, shareholder-loan agreement, tax identification, source-of-funds evidence, UBO information, and proof of the commercial purpose. Retain transfer confirmations, bank statements, corporate resolutions, accounting entries, and any Banco de España statistical or foreign-investment filings applicable to the transaction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area. Use SWIFT cross-border payment messaging, increasingly through ISO 20022 formats, for non-SEPA or non-euro settlements; MT103 remains a commonly recognized legacy customer-credit-transfer reference during bank migration. For documentary trade, use an irrevocable commercial letter of credit governed by UCP 600, with documentary presentation, discrepancy controls, sanctions screening, and bank confirmation where commercially justified. Documentary collections may use URC 522. Match payments to purchase orders, commercial invoices, customs declarations, bills of lading, certificates of origin, insurance documents, and goods-receipt evidence. Apply dual authorization, segregation of duties, beneficiary validation, callback controls for changes, transaction limits, sanctions screening, and three-way reconciliation among contract, invoice, and logistics evidence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards for documented commercial exposures, subject to bank suitability, counterparty-credit, collateral, valuation, confirmation, and EMIR reporting requirements where applicable.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or markets where physical delivery is restricted or impractical, subject to the relevant market's legality, bank approval, settlement controls, sanctions screening, and documentation of the underlying exposure.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for recurring or material currency and funding exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent master documentation, EMIR obligations, collateral terms, valuation controls, and board-approved risk limits.

Foreign-exchange options and collars for asymmetric cash-flow protection, subject to MiFID II client classification, appropriateness or suitability requirements, premium and valuation controls, and documented understanding of contingent obligations.
Natural hedging through matching foreign-currency revenues with procurement, debt service, payroll, or operating expenses in the same currency, supported by a treasury policy and exposure forecast.
Speculative foreign-exchange trading unrelated to identifiable commercial, financing, or balance-sheet exposures should be prohibited under the company's treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to €3,000 and risk of administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Exceeds two of the following: net turnover > €2,500,000, total assets > €1,200,000 or equity > €500,000
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (PGC) or IFRS where applicable

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual filing and confirmation of beneficial ownership information in the Register of Beneficial Owners

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (general; Ley 27/2014 art. 29.1; reduced 15% for newly created SMEs on first EUR 50,000 of taxable base for the first tax period and the following period; minimum 15% effective tax on the pre-offset taxable base applies to groups/entities with net turnover ≥ EUR 20 million)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New-company 15% rate (art. 29.1 LIS) on first taxable base tranche; Reserva de capitalización (10% of equity increase reduces the base, capped at 10% of the base); Reserva de nivelación for SMEs with net turnover < EUR 10 million (10% base reduction, max EUR 1 million, 5-year recycling); R&D and innovation deductions (25%-42%); double-tax relief under art. 21/31 LIS; Patent box (art. 23 LIS).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward (no statutory expiry) — offset capped per annum at 70% of the taxable base (turnover < EUR 20m), 60% (turnover EUR 20m-60m), 50% (turnover ≥ EUR 60m); turnover ≥ EUR 20m entities must still pay tax on at least 15% of the pre-offset base.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (annual Corporate Income Tax return) + Modelo 220 for tax consolidation groups; filed at the Agencia Tributaria's Sede Electrónica (Electronic Office) with a digital certificate; mandatory electronic filing for legal persons.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return (Modelo 200) plus three advance installment payments (pagos fraccionados) filed in April, October and December (1–20 of the calendar month).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200 due within the first 25 calendar days of the sixth month after the tax-period end: a 31-December year-end produces a filing window from 1 to 25 July of the following year. Advance payments are due 1-20 April, 1-20 October and 1-20 December of each period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resultado contable de la cuenta de pérdidas y ganancias (accounting profit or loss per the statutory financial statements before tax).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the resident SL: enter the company's full Spanish P&L result. For a non-resident entity without a PE: not applicable; the Modelo 200 is not filed (income is reported via Modelo 210/216).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ajustes positivos (non-deductible expenses and other positive adjustments to the accounting result, e.g., penalties, non-deductible amortization, 30% EBITDA interest-limitation add-back).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all mandatory add-backs of the resident company; no foreign PE booking is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ajustes negativos (negative adjustments: exempt dividends, tax-free revaluations, reservation deductions such as Reserva de capitalización/nivelación).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only adjustments supported by documentary evidence retained in Spain.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Base imponible (taxable base after offset of prior-year tax losses; loss offset is capped as described above).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offset tax losses only with the corresponding socio-economic continuity and within the 70/60/50% caps.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cuota íntegra (gross tax charge = taxable base × applicable rate: 25% general, 15% new-company tranche, 15% minimum for large groups).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the correct reduced rate eligibility before applying the standard 25%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Retenciones e ingresos a cuenta (withholdings and on-account payments suffered during the year: bank interest, Spanish dividends received, rental income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit is available only to the resident SL; attach certificates (Modelos 193/123) to claim the credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cuota diferencial (result due to the Treasury or to be refunded, after deduction of withholdings, installment payments and carried credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance must be paid at filing; refund requests are processed by AEAT within 6 months, but the SL must not leave outstanding balances.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without a previous AEAT request: 5% (delay ≤ 3 months) / 10% (3-6m) / 15% (6-12m) / 20% (> 12m) surcharge plus daily late-payment interest (4.06% for 2024); fixed fine of EUR 200 when no tax is due; incorrect or incomplete returns: penalty of 50%-150% of the amount; non-filing with AEAT regularisation: 50%-150% plus interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 216 (quarterly withholding-return of the Spanish payor for income paid to non-residents, including dividends, interest and royalties) and annual Modelo 296 (summary); filed via Sede Electrónica.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly (Modelo 216) within the first 20 days of April, July, October and January; annual summary Modelo 296 by 31 January.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly: 1-20 calendar days following the natural quarter. Annual: 1-31 January of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the payment as dividend (1), interest (4), royalty (5), etc.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the income code applicable to the profit distribution to the non-resident shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, tax ID and country of residence of the non-resident recipient, plus the tax residence certificate reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The recipient must provide a valid TRC (with Spanish DGT seal validation where required); claims of DTA or EU-directive exemption must be evidenced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross amount paid, withholding rate applied, and amount of WHT entered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Domestic rate 19%; DTA-reduced rate or 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary / Interest-Royalties directives can be applied only with the TRC and, for EU-directive exemption, a declaration of 12-month holding and ≥ 5% ownership.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Modelo 216: penalty 50%-150% of the tax not withheld; non-withholding when obliged: penalty of 100%-150% of the omitted withholding; late-filing surcharges of 5%-20% plus interest apply as indicated for Modelo 200.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on dividend distributions to non-resident beneficial owners without a PE (IRNR art. 25; Ley 5/2004), unless treaty-reduced; resident Spanish corporate shareholders generally benefit from the 95%-100% exemption under art. 21 LIS.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: (1) Obtain a valid Certification of Tax Residence (TRC) from the shareholder's own tax authority for the relevant fiscal year; (2) Deliver the TRC, an updated holding certificate and, for the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, a declaration of ≥ 5% holding for 12 months to the Spanish paying SL before the dividend payment; (3) The SL applies the reduced/zero rate at source in Modelo 216; (4) If WHT was over-withheld, the non-resident must file Modelo 210 self-assessment to claim the refund within 4 years from the end of the filing period; (5) Spain may cross-verify TRCs via automatic exchange of information / MLI-PPT where abuse is suspected.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory WHT is 19% for both interest and royalties paid to non-residents. Treaty reductions: EU associated companies may access 0% under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive (5% holding where applicable and > 24-month relationship in some cases); most full DTAs reduce interest to 10% (0-10%) and royalties to 0-10% (e.g., 0% for industrial royalties with the US treaty, 8% for patents/trademarks in several LATAM treaties). The same Modelo 216/296 filing protocol and TRC obligations govern source-rate relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Documentación específica (Local File) is mandatory when the taxpayer's related-party transactions during the tax period exceed EUR 250,000 (total volume); where turnover ≥ EUR 10 million, documentation is required regardless of volume? (In practice, companies with turnover ≥ EUR 10 million face the full documentation set; the group Master File (documentación conjunta) is mandatory when the consolidated net turnover of the group reaches EUR 45 million.)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime as in offshore centres; substance operates through general rules: (i) art. 15.h LIS denies deduction of expenses paid to entities in listed tax havens unless the payor proves the transaction is real and the counterparty genuinely carries on economic activities; (ii) art. 15 LGT 'conflicto en la aplicación de la norma' (GAAR) recharacterizes artificial structures; (iii) art. 17 LIS (substance-over-form on valuation of deferred earnings) and (iv) the CFC rules of art. 100 LIS and the MLI Principal Purpose Test protect DTA benefits. The UHT plant's physical staff, production site and packaging equipment constitute strong factual substance that will survive these tests if properly documented.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Criminal Defraudation of the Treasury
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful failure to file Modelo 200, use of false invoices to inflate costs, understatement of taxable profits, or fictitious restructuring to move profits to zero-rate jurisdictions, causing a tax loss to the Spanish Treasury exceeding EUR 120,000 in one fiscal period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Code art. 305: imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and fine of 2-4 times the defrauded amount (2-6 years and 6-fold fine when the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 600,000); loss of subsidies or tax benefits for up to 5 years; public sentencing. Corporate liability under art. 310 bis CP: fine, judicial supervision, and potentially dissolution of the SL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly (solidarily) liable for the tax debt and penalties under LGT art. 42.2(a); criminal conviction of the managing director carries personal imprisonment, disqualification from managing other companies, seizure of passport and travel bans where flight risk exists, and confiscation of assets through civil restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SL having no real personnel, premises or productive activity and being used to issue circular invoices or to channel intangible royalties to an interposed non-resident entity, without 'motivos económicos válidos'.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR (art. 15 LGT): the transaction is declared a 'conflicto en la aplicación de la norma' and taxed per its economic substance, with a specific 50% penalty on the tax avoided (art. 206 bis LGT) and refusal of VAT input deduction; use of false commercial invoices also triggers falsification penalties (art. 283/392 CP) of up to 3 years' imprisonment, and administrative fines up to EUR 150,000 per invoice detail.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing of the corporate veil applies (LGT art. 42; Civil Code doctrine): directors who participated are jointly liable for the whole unpaid debt; if the shell is used for money laundering, the director can be sentenced to 6 months to 6 years' imprisonment, with travel bans pending trial and restitution orders for the funds moved.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation and Arm's Length Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operation of a related-party sale at a manipulated margin (e.g., packaging materials sold to an affiliate in a low-tax country at an inflated price), or failure to prepare the Local/Master File above the EUR 250,000 / EUR 45 million thresholds, or submission of false documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT regularises to the arm's length result with a 50% assessment-penalty (art. 194 LGT; raised to 100%-150% in cases with wilful intent); separate fixed penalty of EUR 1,500 for each data item omitted, false or inaccurate in the TP documentation (art. 198.2 LGT) and EUR 1,000 for documents submitted out of time; interest of 4.06% accrues from the original filing date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign returns knowing that the documentation is false are jointly liable for both the adjustment and the penalty; absent any genuine substance at the foreign counterparty, criminal fraud (art. 305 CP) can be pursued if the total defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, resulting in imprisonment and personal civil restitution.
